public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI industry is producing no real profitability or return on investment.

statement.excerpt: At the same time, the things that they need to happen — actual profitability, actual returns on investment, actual tangible proof that this is a real thing rather than something they all have to actively conspire to keep alive — aren’t happening at all.

from_speaker: actual tangible proof that this is a real thing
our_interpretation: The plain reading is categorical: AI businesses are not producing actual profits, and customers are not realizing positive financial returns from AI.
I use January–March 2026, the latest completed common calendar quarter before the May 26 post. This is an evaluator choice because the sentence describes an ongoing state without dates.

Relevant profit and return evidence must isolate AI activity and account for the relevant costs. Broad company or cloud profits, revenue growth, and gross productivity savings are insufficient by themselves.
The tangible-proof phrase reinforces the financial assertion; I do not create a separate test for whether AI is real.
The quote supplies no accounting basis. Under the supplied money-claim rule, unknown basis prevents a supported or contradicted score.
criteria.support_condition: Comprehensive, comparable evidence establishes no positive AI-specific profits or realized positive financial returns in the target period. Losses at a few AI labs cannot establish this industry-wide absence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one documented AI-specific positive profit or realized positive financial return in the target period refutes the categorical absence, provided company, period, metric, and accounting basis match the contract.
